correctness.rationale: Admissible ideal/filter pairs give an exact bijection and product-plus-mixed polynomial for all finite disjoint-chain parameter posets. Coefficients for two chains admit a verified three-region form; explicit boundary inequalities prove the unimodality and log-concavity if-and-only-if criteria at all lengths. Exact exhaustive partition and independent ternary enumeration through size eight prove the sharp global first cases, while symbolic witness families cover every larger size. The self-contained checker returns VERIFY_OK; finite tests are not substituted for infinite claims.

originality.rationale: The graded comparability coefficients and sharp shape boundaries are not consequences of the ungraded ideal/filter type-count formula, scalar incomparability-sensitive lower bound, or linear-extension descent unimodality. Statement-level comparisons used the full RESULT.md of the published 2026 lower-bound result, the primary §3 text of Cameron–Nešetřil, Pach et al. and Knauer et al. §4, together with semantic research-index searches and primary literature comparisons. The first missing shapes are checked by exhaustive finite certificates. Residual risk: unindexed equivalent work and incomplete direct inspection of Simion (1984). Also inspected the 2025/2026 Kwiatkowska–Sullivan–Winkel full article: its main theorem is about uniquely extensible embeddings, despite using exterior type triples.
residual_risks: A logically equivalent graded comparability polynomial could appear in unindexed poset literature or be an implicit corollary of a broader combinatorial enumeration not identified by the searches.
Simion (1984) primary full text was not directly inspected; later full-text treatment pins down its distinct descent statistic.
Finite first-threshold census has exact source code but has not undergone independent human review.

value.rationale: A complete all-size coefficient-shape classification for two nonempty chains, sharp first nonunimodality and non-log-concavity among arbitrary disjoint-chain profiles, unique minimum witnesses and persistent infinite obstructions yield precise new information on a natural extension-type invariant. Unlike an arbitrary isolated coefficient, this measures intrinsic regularity of type distributions and contrasts with classical real-rooted linear-extension descent statistics; the existing ungraded scalar theorem leaves this question unanswered.
